summary.oneLiner: OnMobile is a 25-year-old diversified digital lifestyle platform for telecom operators, spanning mobile/console gaming, AI-powered enterprise communications, and mobile entertainment (Ringback Tones, video, infotainment), and is the global leader in Ringback Tones.

currentContext.strengths: Global leader in Ringback Tones with a 25-year operating history across 2G/3G/4G/5G/AI technology cycles|Operator relationships averaging over a decade across 67 operators, giving deployment speed and distribution reach the company describes as very difficult to replicate from scratch|Telco-integrated distribution model for Buzzmo gives access to enterprise (BFSI) deployments that flow through operator channels, a path most standalone CPaaS providers lack|ONMO streaming patents, including AI-driven streaming and 'snackable moments' gaming, underpinning the Virtual Console/Smart Console product|Accumulated consumer and telco insights (from two decades of Ringback Tones/Video/Contest services) that funded the strategic pivot into gaming in 2021
currentContext.strategies: Expand the gaming business beyond mobile into the console market via the ONMO+ Smart Console, an affordable console-quality cloud gaming solution|Open new commercial/distribution channels beyond traditional telecom partnerships for Smart Console - e-commerce platforms, retail chains, broadband providers, TV and cable operators|Use India and Spain as initial Smart Console markets to gather consumer-behaviour and ARPU insights ahead of broader expansion into the Middle East, Asia, Africa and Americas|Broaden B2B partnerships to introduce Smart Console to new markets and customer segments|Strengthen gaming marketing through AI-driven forecasting and planning, and expand into new channels and formats|Expand Buzzmo's presence in Africa, where mobile penetration, financial inclusion and enterprise demand are converging into a single commercial opportunity|Diversify OnMobile's revenue base by growing gaming and enterprise communications (Buzzmo) alongside the legacy entertainment business|Maintain prudent capital allocation, directing investment toward technology, product capabilities and infrastructure that support long-term scalability while preserving financial discipline|Use leasing arrangements for gaming servers and Smart Console controllers (the two largest variable costs of customer growth) to reduce future capital requirements while scaling|Restore historical collection cycles / DSO to prior levels as a management priority|Continue deepening investment in automation, AI-driven monitoring and intelligent engineering tools (OARM, AIOps, MLOps) to drive operational and executional efficiency|Expand the premium gaming catalogue on ONMO and enhance player engagement through differentiated gaming experiences|Stabilise the video and editorial businesses through newly implemented contracts while contributing new revenue streams
currentContext.expansion: OnMobile's expansion is platform/product-led rather than physical-asset-led. FY26 saw the commercial launch of the ONMO+ Smart Console, the culmination of six years of investment in gaming architecture, cloud infrastructure, subscriber management/billing, and streaming/content-delivery technology; during the year the team completed final commercialisation components including AAA cloud-streaming technology integration, optimised server architecture on AMD gaming GPUs, and a multi-device pro controller. Initial rollout covers India and (before year-end) Spain via retail distribution, with the company preparing broader expansion of the Smart Console across the Middle East, Asia, Africa and the Americas, and into new non-telecom distribution channels (e-commerce platforms, retail chains, broadband providers, TV/cable operators). The Gaming & Entertainment Platform (TGEP) expanded its operator footprint by signing Robi in Bangladesh during FY26 and has three additional operator opportunities in advanced stages of closure for FY27. The Tones business is developing a next-generation cloud-native CRBT platform for greater scalability and carrier-grade performance, with first production deployment scheduled for Q2 FY27, and expanded footprint via a brownfield deployment with Claro Peru and a greenfield deployment with Safaricom in Ethiopia. No physical plant, manufacturing capacity or site-based capex is disclosed; the company operates one national office (Bengaluru) and ten overseas branch offices, consistent with an asset-light services/platform model.

OnMobile differentiates via its AI layer, telco-integrated delivery and emerging-market focus|The Gaming & Entertainment Platform (TGEP) has three additional operator deployment opportunities in advanced stages of closure, positioning it to expand its operator footprint in FY27|Buzzmo secured a multi-year contract with Vodafone Qatar to power enterprise communication and customer engagement, strengthening its presence in the Middle East telecom segment|Buzzmo enables over 1,000 enterprise clients through a decade-long partnership with a leading Middle East operator|TGEP expanded its operator footprint during the year by signing with Robi in Bangladesh|Tones expanded within the America Movil group via a brownfield deployment with Claro Peru (adding an existing subscriber base of approximately 90,000 users), and via a greenfield deployment with Safaricom in Ethiopia that grew to over 750,000 subscribers within eight months of launch|The Emocion contract with Telefonica Spain (originally set to expire in July 2026) was transitioned via addendum into a yearly auto-renewal arrangement, strengthening continuity and visibility for the infotainment business

risks.note: Revenue is earned through revenue-sharing arrangements with telco partners across markets; while this partner network is a competitive strength, it also exposes the business to unilateral commercial changes by partners that affect revenue economics and deployment timelines.

risks.risk: Structural decline of legacy entertainment services
risks.note: OTT calling and music streaming are reducing the relevance of Ringback Tones in developed markets, with consumer preferences shifting to on-demand, self-directed content; content licensing arrangements also remain subject to unilateral partner changes that can affect margins, requiring careful commercial/product discipline to manage the transition.

risks.risk: Geopolitical, regulatory and macroeconomic exposure across a large operating footprint
risks.note: Operations across 69 countries carry regulatory, technological, operational and macroeconomic risks; an unsettled geopolitical environment and ongoing conflicts create uncertainty around inflation, supply-chain disruption and commodity cost pressures.

Currency volatility across the Company's 69 operating countries adds further unpredictability to earnings; the Company carries material net foreign-currency denominated monetary assets/liabilities (USD, EUR and other currencies) and uses forward contracts to hedge part of this exposure.

risks.risk: Intense competition for consumer attention / willingness-to-pay erosion
risks.note: The most fundamental threat in digital lifestyle services is the consumer's attention span - gaming and entertainment platforms compete with social media, short-form video, OTT and messaging apps for a fixed daily time budget; free-to-access models erode willingness to pay even as production costs rise.
Rising GPU and memory-chip costs, driven by demand for AI infrastructure, are creating potential supply constraints specific to the cloud/console gaming business (Virtual Console / Smart Console).

Enterprise communication is a mature industry with entrenched incumbents, large traffic aggregators and CPaaS platforms competing aggressively on price and scale; protecting share against well-capitalised competitors is described as a sustained effort.

risks.risk: Tightening AI, data-privacy and digital-payments regulation
risks.note: Global frameworks governing AI, data privacy, enterprise messaging and digital payments are tightening, and enforcement actions in key markets could disrupt monetisation or delay deployments; billing transparency around subscription confirmations/auto-renewals remains a focus given its impact on consumer trust and brand equity.
